title: Sentinel observability module: automated rolling upgrades, canary health checks, and multi-tenant log shippers
creator: Ava Park
description:
Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module (module path: redwood/observability/sentinel) that provisions a production-ready observability stack for VPC/private deployments. The stack includes Prometheus (server + remote_write), Grafana (with provisioning + datasource dashboards), an OpenTelemetry Collector deployment, and a configurable log-shipping agent (Vector or Fluentd) that ships logs to customer S3 or a central logging tier. The module must: 1) support zero-downtime rolling upgrades with automatic canary promotion/rollback driven by health-check metrics; 2) be parameterized for multi-tenant namespaces and RBAC; 3) allow encrypted artifact storage (KMS) and fine-grained network controls (security groups, private subnets); 4) emit stable outputs for Console integration (prometheus_endpoint, grafana_url, otel_endpoint, log_shipper_topic).

Design highlights and decisions: 
- Provisioning model: Terraform module will use Helm provider for chart installs (prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack, grafana/grafana, otel/collector). For log shipping, we support Vector by default with a Fluentd opt-in flag.
- Upgrade strategy: Chart upgrades are executed via Helm release resource with explicitly set upgrade parameters: max_unavailable=0, max_surge=1, and a post-upgrade canary check pipeline. We will implement a canary namespace pattern: promote N% of scrape targets to new release and evaluate metrics (scrape_success_ratio >= 99.5%, alert_rate <= baseline + 0.5%). If checks fail within grace period, the CI/CD workflow triggers an automatic rollback using Helm's rollback command.
- Health checks & metrics gating: Canary promotion is gated by a short-lived Prometheus query (configured in the module as canary_queries) and an external health-runner (implemented as a small GH Action and a kubernetes job) that polls success/error metrics and log errors.
- Secrets & encryption: Grafana admin creds and otel TLS certs are optional inputs as secret ARNs; when provided, the module will wire secrets via KMS-encrypted Secret Manager/SSM or Kubernetes ExternalSecrets depending on the hosting environment.
- Networking: All resources respect provided VPC IDs, subnets, and private security groups. LoadBalancers will default to internal-only and support NLB for prometheus remote-write receiver endpoints.
- Migration path: For existing customers we provide a side-by-side deployment pattern: deploy new sentinel namespace, configure temporary remote_write to stream into both old and new Prometheus, compare retention and scrape fidelity for 72 hours, then cut over traffic and decommission the old stack.

Module Inputs (examples): cluster_id, namespace, vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, prometheus_retention_days, grafana_admin_secret_arn, otel_collector_config_yaml, log_shipper_type (vector|fluentd), s3_log_bucket, s3_kms_key_arn, iam_role_arns, canary_percentage, canary_queries.

Module Outputs (examples): prometheus_endpoint, grafana_url, grafana_admin_secret_arn, otel_collector_endpoint, log_shipper_sqs_topic_arn, helm_release_ids.

Compatibility: Module must support EKS (helm/kube), AKS (helm/kube) and generic k8s-on-prem (helm + nodeport/internal LB). The implementation will prefer generic Helm usage and limit cloud-specific resources to optional submodules (aws_logs_bridge, azure_blob_bridge).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Terraform plan/apply can successfully create the stack in a lab VPC with provided creds. 
- Canary promotion pipeline performs automatic verification and can rollback within configured windows. 
- Grafana is provisioned with at least two dashboards (cluster health, telemetry ingestion) and datasource pointing to the module's Prometheus. 
- Logs from app namespace are ingested and visible in the configured destination (S3 or central logging). 
- Documented runbook for upgrades, rollback, and emergency shutdown included in the repo README and Redwood Console integration notes.

Related docs & artifacts: initial design doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sentinel-design; helm charts considered: https://github.com/prometheus-helm/charts and https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-helm-charts; initial proto repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-observability-sentinel
